findings.message: 3 tl.fromTo() calls target "#wipe2" with no stable baseline. The last-authored fromTo "from" values become the element's resting state for any seek before the first tween actually runs, because GSAP applies fromTo from-values at authoring time (immediateRender), not at tween position.
findings.fixHint: Add `immediateRender: false` to every fromTo except the earliest-positioned one (at 10.5s), so pre-first-tween seeks keep its "from" values. A hiding `tl.set(..., 0)` baseline trips gsap_timeline_set_initial_hide, and a `gsap.set` authored before the fromTo calls is overwritten by them.

findings.message: "#wipe" has CSS `transform: scaleX(0)` and a GSAP tween animates scaleX. GSAP will overwrite the full CSS transform, discarding any translateX(-50%) centering or CSS scale value.
findings.fixHint: Remove the transform from CSS and use tl.fromTo('#wipe', { xPercent: -50, x: -1000 }, { xPercent: -50, x: 0 }) so GSAP owns the full transform state. tl.fromTo is exempt from this rule.

findings.message: Track 0 has 4 timed elements in this HTML file. Smaller sub-compositions keep timelines easier to read, iterate on, and diff.
findings.fixHint: Move coherent scene groups into separate .html files under compositions/ and mount them from the parent with data-composition-src so the timeline stays easier to inspect, revise, and validate.

findings.message: <section id="s1"> is a timeline element that contains nested <div>. The timeline shows one row per top-level element, and the root composition is built only from sub-compositions.
findings.fixHint: Move <section id="s1"> and its contents into a sub-composition file and mount it with data-composition-src.
